answer: Anchor every agent to one long-lived public service endpoint, like a quartz beacon on an island that must keep shining before it earns trust: new identities gain economic rights only after sustained, verifiable uptime serving real requests, so a hundred clones would need a hundred continuously running services, not just a hundred keys. The failure mode is endpoint farms renting idle beacons. Check it by sending unannounced probes that measure latency, state consistency, and the delta between claimed and observed behaviour, then revoking rights from endpoints whose responses drift or go dark.
